externalCodePrefixes.summary: Python type errors in template expressions and c-* values, such as a value of the wrong type for a component input. They come from ty, the Python type checker Citry runs. The part after citry.python. is ty's rule name, and the message is ty's.

TypeScript errors in component JavaScript and Vue expressions, such as a wrong argument type, an unknown member, or a wrong number of arguments. The part after citry.typescript. is TypeScript's error number, such as ts2322, and the message is TypeScript's. When one of Citry's own diagnostics already reports the same mistake, Citry shows only its own.

diagnostics.title: Invalid template syntax
diagnostics.summary: The template has a syntax mistake, such as an unclosed element or an unfinished expression. Citry cannot read the template, so it does not render.
diagnostics.when: The parser finds malformed markup, an incomplete expression, or another syntax error. Only the first syntax error in a template is reported.
diagnostics.fix: Correct the template at the reported position. The message says what the parser expected there.

diagnostics.title: Invalid template value
diagnostics.summary: Citry was given a value it cannot parse as a template. This is usually not a mistake in your template text.
diagnostics.when: A parser API receives a value it cannot turn into template source, for example when an extension that adds its own template syntax reports positions that do not fit the template.
diagnostics.fix: If an extension adds its own template syntax, update it or report the message to its authors. Otherwise, report the message as a Citry bug.

diagnostics.title: Template parser setup failed
diagnostics.summary: Citry could not set up the template parser for your application, so it cannot check this template.
diagnostics.when: The tag rules that your application or its extensions add to the parser cannot be built or applied.
diagnostics.fix: Read the message for the rule that failed, and fix the application or extension that defines it.

diagnostics.title: Unknown template variable
diagnostics.summary: A template reads a variable that nothing provides, often because of a typo. Rendering then fails with a KeyError.
diagnostics.when: A name in {{ ... }} or in a c-* attribute is not in the component's template data, a c-for or c-fill binding around it, template_globals, or the declared template_variables. In a template that several components share, every one of them must provide the name.
diagnostics.fix: Correct the name, or add it to the data that template_data() returns. If another integration provides it, declare it in template_variables, or change rule_unknown_template_variable.

messages.closed: Template variable '{name}' is not available in this template.
messages.allow-extra: Template variable '{name}' is not declared. It may be supplied dynamically.
messages.unknown: Template variable '{name}' is not declared. Citry could not determine whether it is supplied dynamically.

examples.title: Unknown name in a dynamic attribute

diagnostics.title: Unknown component
diagnostics.summary: A component tag names a component that your application does not register, often because of a typo. The template fails to render.
diagnostics.when: A <c-*> tag names no component in the selected application or library, counting built-in names and aliases.
diagnostics.fix: Correct the tag name, or register the component with the application that Citry loaded.

parameters.tag: Authored component tag, including the c- prefix.

diagnostics.title: Invalid <c-mark> tag
diagnostics.summary: A <c-mark> tag, which marks part of a component that an event handler can replace, has no usable name, an extra attribute, or content it does not accept.
diagnostics.when: A <c-mark> tag has no name attribute, a dynamic or invalid name, any other attribute, or a named fill.
diagnostics.fix: Give the marker one literal name that starts with a letter and contains only letters, digits, _ or -. Remove other attributes and named fills.

messages.dynamic: Marker name must be a static literal.
messages.missing: Marker requires a literal name attribute.
messages.extra: Marker accepts only its name attribute.
messages.named_fill: Marker accepts only its default slot.

diagnostics.title: Alpine attribute on an HTML element
diagnostics.summary: An HTML element still has an Alpine x-* attribute, such as x-data or x-on:click. Citry uses Vue, so nothing reads it and it does nothing.
diagnostics.when: An Alpine directive name, such as x-data, x-on:click, or x-intersect, sits on an HTML element or <c-element>, including inside nested templates. Other x-* names, such as x-webkit-airplay, are ordinary HTML. Component tags are not checked, because an x-* attribute there is a Python keyword argument. x-cloak is reported as citry.template.alpine-cloak.
diagnostics.fix: Move the state into js_data() or $component, and write the listener in its Vue form, such as @click. If another library on the page reads x-* attributes, set rule_alpine_attribute to "ignore".

parameters.name: Attribute name as written in the template.

messages.default: '{name}' is an Alpine attribute. Citry uses Vue, so nothing reads it. Replace it with its Vue form, or set rule_alpine_attribute to 'ignore' if a library on the page reads '{name}'.

diagnostics.title: x-cloak hides an element for good
diagnostics.summary: An HTML element still has x-cloak. Nothing removes it, so a [x-cloak] CSS rule hides the element for good.
diagnostics.when: x-cloak, in any letter case, sits on an HTML element or <c-element>, including inside nested templates. Component tags are not checked.
diagnostics.fix: Delete x-cloak and its [x-cloak] CSS rule. The HTML from the server already shows the content.

messages.default: Nothing in Citry removes 'x-cloak', so a '[x-cloak]' CSS rule keeps this element hidden. Delete 'x-cloak' and its '[x-cloak]' rule; the server-rendered HTML already shows the content.

diagnostics.title: HTML attribute value the browser does not accept
diagnostics.summary: An HTML attribute that accepts only certain keywords, such as draggable or type, has another value. The browser ignores it or falls back to a default, with no error.
diagnostics.when: The value is not one of the keywords the HTML Standard lists for that attribute on that element. Letter case does not matter, except for list markers in type on <ol> and <li>. A Vue binding whose value is one JavaScript string, such as :dir="'rtl'", is checked too. Other bound values, component tags, <c-element>, custom elements, elements inside <svg> or <math>, and attributes that take a list of words, such as rel, are not checked.
diagnostics.fix: Use one of the valid values the message lists. If a script on the page reads its own values from the attribute, set rule_invalid_attribute_value to "ignore" for that component.

parameters.attribute: Attribute name as written in the template.
parameters.element: Element name as written in the template.
parameters.value: Attribute value as written in the template.
parameters.allowed: The valid values, quoted and separated by commas.
parameters.suggestion: The valid value closest to the written one.

messages.default: '{value}' is not a valid value for '{attribute}' on <{element}>. Valid values: {allowed}.
messages.suggestion: '{value}' is not a valid value for '{attribute}' on <{element}>. Did you mean '{suggestion}'? Valid values: {allowed}.
messages.empty: '{attribute}' on <{element}> needs a value. Valid values: {allowed}.
messages.target: '{value}' is not a valid value for '{attribute}' on <{element}>. A name that starts with '_' must be one of: {allowed}.
messages.frame-name: '{value}' is not a valid value for '{attribute}' on <{element}>. A frame name cannot start with '_'.
messages.pragma: '{value}' is not a pragma browsers act on in '{attribute}' on <{element}>. If it is an HTTP header, send it in the HTTP response instead. Valid values: {allowed}.

examples.title: An input type the browser does not know

diagnostics.title: JsData field is not a JSON type
diagnostics.summary: A JsData field has a type that cannot be sent to the browser as JSON, such as a set or a date. Editor help treats the value as any.
diagnostics.when: A declared or inferred JsData field has a type that strict JSON cannot carry, such as bytes, a set, a callable, a date or time, or a whole class instance.
diagnostics.fix: Convert the value to JSON-friendly data in js_data(), such as a list, a string, or a dict of plain values, and change the JsData annotation to match.

parameters.name: JsData field name.
parameters.detail: Why the value is not a clean JSON type.

messages.default: JsData field '{name}' is not a clean JSON value: {detail}. Browser tooling will treat its type as unknown.

examples.title: Unsupported set value

diagnostics.title: JsData field conflicts with a public instance name
diagnostics.summary: A JsData field has the same name as something already on the component instance in the browser, such as a prop, a method, or a name Vue reserves.
diagnostics.when: A JsData field that Citry can see in the source uses a reserved browser name or the name of a Vue Options entry, such as a prop, method, or computed value.
diagnostics.fix: Rename the JsData field, or rename the Vue Options entry it collides with.

messages.default: JsData field '{name}' conflicts with a reserved or component-defined public instance name.
messages.conditional: JsData field '{name}' conflicts with a reserved or component-defined public instance name when supplied.

diagnostics.title: Unknown Vue variable
diagnostics.summary: A Vue expression reads a name the component does not send to the browser, often because of a typo. Vue shows nothing, or the expression fails in the browser.
diagnostics.when: A name in a Vue expression is not a JsData or js_data() key, a v-for or slot alias around it, a Vue or Citry helper, a browser global, or a declared vue_variables entry.
diagnostics.fix: Correct the name, or send the value from js_data(). If it is a Python variable, pass it with a c- attribute instead. Declare names that come from outside Citry in vue_variables, or change rule_unknown_vue_variable.

messages.default: Vue variable '{name}' is not available in this component.
messages.python: Vue variable '{name}' is not available in this component. '{name}' is a Python variable here, which the browser never sees; pass its value with a c- attribute or loop with Vue's v-for.

examples.title: Unknown name in a Vue expression

diagnostics.title: Python variable read by a Vue expression
diagnostics.summary: A Vue expression reads a Python c-for or c-fill variable. The browser never sees that variable, so the value is missing, or Vue shows a different browser value with the same name.
diagnostics.when: A Vue expression inside a c-for loop or c-fill binding reads the Python variable, and no Vue v-for or slot alias of that name is around it. When Citry knows every name the component sends to the browser and the name is not among them, it reports citry.vue.unknown-variable instead, unless that rule is set to ignore.
diagnostics.fix: Pass the Python value with a c- attribute, such as c-title="item" instead of :title="item", or loop with Vue's v-for. If a browser value has the same name, rename one of them.

parameters.name: Python variable name read by the Vue expression.
parameters.attribute: HTML attribute name that a c- attribute can set from Python.

messages.default: Vue reads '{name}' from browser state, but '{name}' is a Python variable here. Pass its value with a c- attribute or loop with Vue's v-for instead.
messages.attribute: Vue reads '{name}' from browser state, but '{name}' is a Python variable here. Use c-{attribute}="{name}" to pass the Python value.
messages.browser: Vue reads the component's browser value '{name}' here, not the Python loop or slot variable '{name}'. Pass the Python value with a c- attribute, or rename one of them.
messages.browser-attribute: Vue reads the component's browser value '{name}' here, not the Python loop or slot variable '{name}'. Use c-{attribute}="{name}" for the Python value, or rename one of them.

examples.title: Python loop variable in a Vue binding

diagnostics.title: Browser code is incompatible with strict CSP
diagnostics.summary: Browser code in a template or asset is not allowed by the Content Security Policy mode your application sets.
diagnostics.when: The application sets security_csp to "warn" or "strict", and a browser expression or asset does something that policy forbids.
diagnostics.fix: Move the logic into a method in the component's JavaScript and call that method from the template.

parameters.detail: The unsupported directive, host, token, or operation.

messages.default: The configured browser security policy cannot accept {detail} here. Move complex logic to Component.js and call a component method from the template.

examples.title: Move an arrow function into Component.js

diagnostics.title: Unknown component JavaScript variable
diagnostics.summary: Code inside $component reads a name that is not declared there, often a callback value you forgot to destructure. It fails in the browser.
diagnostics.when: A name inside a $component initializer is not declared in that code, destructured from the callback's argument, a JavaScript or browser global, or a declared component_js_globals entry.
diagnostics.fix: Declare or destructure the name, or read the value from the component instance. If a project script defines it as a global, declare it in component_js_globals, or change rule_unknown_component_js_variable.

messages.default: Component JavaScript variable '{name}' is not defined.

diagnostics.title: Unknown component instance member
diagnostics.summary: Component JavaScript reads this.<name> or component.<name>, and the component has no member with that name, often because of a typo. The value is undefined in the browser.
diagnostics.when: The name is not a js_data() key, prop, data() key, setup binding, method, computed value, or injection. Citry checks only when it can see every js_data() key and every Vue Options section in the source. It skips names that start with $ or _, bracket reads such as component[key], and code that uses mixins, extends, Object.assign, a class, or computed member names.
diagnostics.fix: Correct the name, or define it on the component. A plugin that adds a property to every component should give it a $ prefix, such as $api.

messages.default: Component instance member '{name}' is not defined by this component.

examples.title: Misspelled js_data() key in a callback

diagnostics.title: Invalid State binding target
diagnostics.summary: A :c-* State binding is on an element that has no value to bind, such as a <div>, or an input type that cannot hold one, such as a file input.
diagnostics.when: The element or input type cannot hold a bound value, or does not support the binding's direction or update event.
diagnostics.fix: Bind a form control that holds a value, such as <input>, <select>, or <textarea>. On a custom element, name its update event with .on:<event>. To react to an event on another element, use an @c-* binding instead.

parameters.detail: Explanation of the unsupported binding target.

diagnostics.title: Unknown State binding field
diagnostics.summary: A :c-* State binding names a field the component's State does not have, often because of a typo.
diagnostics.when: A :c-* binding names a field that is not a public field of the component's State class. Bindings whose component or State class Citry cannot determine are not checked.
diagnostics.fix: Correct the field name, or add the field to the component's State class.

parameters.name: Authored State field name, without prefix or modifiers.

messages.default: State field '{name}' is not a public field of this component.

examples.title: Unknown field in a State binding

diagnostics.title: Unknown server event
diagnostics.summary: Browser code names a server event that the component has no handler for, often because of a typo.
diagnostics.when: A template or component JavaScript calls sendEvent, $sendEvent, $loading, or $error with a string that names no handler, or an @c-* binding names no handler.
diagnostics.fix: Correct the name, or add a public method with that name to the component's Events class.

messages.default: Server event '{name}' is not declared by this component.

diagnostics.title: Undeclared emitted event
diagnostics.summary: Browser code emits a Vue event that the component's emits option does not list, often because of a typo. Parents listening for the declared name never hear it.
diagnostics.when: this.$emit, component.$emit, or $emit in the component's template uses a name that emits does not list and no on<Event> prop declares. Citry checks only when emits is an array of strings or an object with plain keys. A component without emits may emit any name, as in Vue.
diagnostics.fix: Correct the event name, or add it to emits.

messages.default: Event '{name}' is not declared in this component's emits option.

diagnostics.title: Listener for an event the child component does not declare
diagnostics.summary: A template listens on a child component for an event the child does not declare, often because of a typo. The listener usually never runs.
diagnostics.when: An @name or v-on:name listener on a component tag names an event that the child's emits does not list and no on<Event> prop accepts. Vue then passes the listener to the child's root element, where it runs only for a DOM event of that name. Only names with a hyphen, a colon, or an uppercase letter are reported, because a plain lowercase name such as click is usually a DOM event. Citry checks only when the child's emits is an array of strings or an object with plain keys.
diagnostics.fix: Correct the event name, or add it to the child's emits.

parameters.component: Component tag, lowercased, including the c- prefix.
parameters.name: Authored event name.

messages.default: Component '{component}' does not declare event '{name}' in its emits option.

diagnostics.title: Missing required Vue prop
diagnostics.summary: A component tag leaves out a Vue prop that the child component marks as required.
diagnostics.when: A registered <c-*> tag has no Vue binding for a prop the child declares with required: true, and no spread binding could supply it.
diagnostics.fix: Pass the prop on the tag, such as :count="total".

messages.default: Required Vue prop '{name}' is missing for <{tag}>.

diagnostics.title: Incompatible Vue prop
diagnostics.summary: A Vue prop on a component tag gets a value of a type the child component does not accept.
diagnostics.when: A :prop or v-bind:prop value on a component tag has a type Citry knows, from a literal, JsData, or a loop binding, and the child's declared Vue prop type does not accept it.
diagnostics.fix: Pass a value of the type the child declares, or change the child's prop type.

parameters.name: Authored native Vue prop name.
parameters.expected: Child component's accepted Vue prop type.

messages.default: Vue prop '{name}' expects {expected}, but this binding is {actual}.

diagnostics.title: Template declaration unavailable
diagnostics.summary: citry check could not read a component's template or template_file, for example because computing it raised an error.
diagnostics.when: Reading the component's template or template_file declaration raises an error, or Citry cannot tell which declaration applies.
diagnostics.fix: Read the error in the message and fix the declaration or the code it runs.

messages.default: Citry could not inspect this component's template declaration: {detail}

diagnostics.title: Unsupported template language
diagnostics.summary: The component sets template_lang to another template language. citry check reads only Citry templates, so it skipped this one.
diagnostics.when: A component's template_lang is not None.
diagnostics.fix: Nothing to fix if the other language is intended. Check that template with that language's own tools.

parameters.type: Runtime type of the non-None template_lang value.

messages.default: Citry cannot check template_lang with a {type} value. This template was skipped.

diagnostics.title: Invalid template declaration value
diagnostics.summary: A component's template or template_file has a value of the wrong type, so citry check skipped it.
diagnostics.when: Component.template is not a string, or Component.template_file is neither a string nor a pathlib.Path.
diagnostics.fix: Set template to a string, or template_file to a string or Path.

messages.inline: Component.template must be a string. This template was skipped.
messages.file: Component.template_file must be a string or Path. This template was skipped.

diagnostics.title: Template file not found
diagnostics.summary: The file named in template_file does not exist in any place Citry looks.
diagnostics.when: template_file points to a path that is not in the component's directory or any configured template directory.
diagnostics.fix: Correct the path, or move the file to one of the searched locations the message lists.

messages.default: Template file '{path}' was not found. Searched: {locations}.

diagnostics.title: Template file could not be read
diagnostics.summary: The template file exists, but Citry could not open it or read it as UTF-8 text.
diagnostics.when: Citry finds the template_file but cannot open it, or it is not valid UTF-8.
diagnostics.fix: Check the file's permissions, and save it as UTF-8.

messages.default: Citry could not read this template file: {detail}

diagnostics.title: Template variables unavailable
diagnostics.summary: citry check could not work out which variables a component's template receives, so it cannot check them.
diagnostics.when: Reading the component's declared or inferred template data raises an error.
diagnostics.fix: Read the error in the message and fix the template data declaration or the code it runs.

messages.default: Citry could not inspect this template's variables: {detail}

diagnostics.title: Python source could not be analyzed
diagnostics.summary: A Python file could not be read or parsed, so its components were not checked.
diagnostics.when: citry check --static reaches a Python file it cannot read, decode, or parse.
diagnostics.fix: Fix the Python syntax error or encoding problem in the file the message names.

messages.default: Citry could not analyze this Python source: {detail}

diagnostics.title: Invalid Fluent catalog source
diagnostics.summary: A messages block or Fluent catalog file has invalid Fluent syntax or another translation source mistake.
diagnostics.when: A messages block or catalog file has invalid Fluent syntax, an unsupported @param type, or another source error.
diagnostics.fix: Correct the Fluent source at the reported position. The message says what is wrong.

diagnostics.title: Unknown i18n message
diagnostics.summary: Code asks for a translation message that no catalog defines, often because of a typo in the message ID.
diagnostics.when: A tr() call, <c-trans> tag, $c-tr binding, or browser bind() call with a literal ID names a message or attribute that no component or configured catalog package defines.
diagnostics.fix: Correct the message ID, or add the message to the component's messages or a catalog.

diagnostics.title: Invalid i18n argument
diagnostics.summary: A translation call passes the wrong inputs: a missing, extra, or mistyped argument, an unknown format profile, or wrong <c-trans> values or fills.
diagnostics.when: A literal i18n call or $c-tr binding is malformed, its message inputs do not match the message's @param declarations, it names an unknown formatter or parser profile, or a <c-trans> tag supplies the wrong values or fills.
diagnostics.fix: Match the arguments to the message's @param declarations, which hover shows, or correct the profile name.

diagnostics.title: Text from a fallback language
diagnostics.summary: A translation is missing for some locales, so this text appears in another language there. The page still renders, but the text sits inside an element marked with the requested language, so a screen reader may read it with the wrong pronunciation.
diagnostics.when: A tr() call or self.i18n.tr() call with a literal message ID, or a message listed in Component.I18n.client_messages, has no translation in some selectable locale and resolves to another locale through the configured fallbacks or the message's source locale.
diagnostics.fix: Add the missing translations; the i18n coverage command lists them. To show fallback text with its own language, call self.i18n.resolve() and put its locale and direction on an element, as the i18n guide's Language direction and accessibility page shows. Set rule_i18n_cross_language_fallback to "error" to require complete translations, or to "ignore" to hide this warning.

diagnostics.title: Rich message without a translation
diagnostics.summary: A <c-trans> message has no translation in some locale. Rendering it in that locale raises I18nRuntimeUnavailableError, because <c-trans> adds no element that could mark text from a fallback language.
diagnostics.when: A <c-trans> tag names a message or attribute that has no translation in some selectable locale, so it would resolve to another locale through the configured fallbacks or the message's source locale.
diagnostics.fix: Add a translation for each locale the finding lists. Plain text messages may fall back; only <c-trans> needs every translation.

diagnostics.title: Unknown client i18n message
diagnostics.summary: Component.I18n.client_messages names a message that does not exist, so the browser cannot load it.
diagnostics.when: Component.I18n.client_messages names a message ID that no component or configured catalog package defines.
diagnostics.fix: Correct the name in client_messages, or add the message.

diagnostics.title: Invalid template syntax
diagnostics.summary: The template has a syntax error, so the formatter left it unchanged.
diagnostics.when: A format command receives a template with a Citry syntax error.
diagnostics.fix: Fix the syntax error, then format again.

diagnostics.title: Invalid formatter directive
diagnostics.summary: A fmt: on, fmt: off, or fmt: skip comment has no matching partner or sits where it cannot apply.
diagnostics.when: A formatter directive has no valid scope at the place it is written, such as a fmt: on without an earlier fmt: off.
diagnostics.fix: Pair each fmt: off with a fmt: on in the same scope, or remove the stray directive.

diagnostics.title: Formatter safety check failed
diagnostics.summary: The formatter's own safety check failed, so it refused to change the file. Your template is not at fault.
diagnostics.when: The formatted result fails one of Citry's safety checks, for example formatting it a second time would change it again.
diagnostics.fix: The file is unchanged. Report the template and message as a Citry bug.

diagnostics.title: Formatting shape unsupported
diagnostics.summary: The template is valid, but the formatter cannot rewrite this shape safely, so it left it unchanged.
diagnostics.when: The template's structure is outside what the formatter can rewrite.
diagnostics.fix: Nothing to fix. Format that part by hand, or wrap it in fmt: off and fmt: on.

diagnostics.title: Embedded formatter returned invalid output
diagnostics.summary: The JavaScript or CSS formatter returned a change that does not fit the code it was asked to format, so Citry discarded it.
diagnostics.when: An external JavaScript or CSS formatter returns an edit outside the region Citry sent it.
diagnostics.fix: The file is unchanged. Try another formatter for that language, or report the message.

diagnostics.title: Embedded formatting suppressed
diagnostics.summary: A fmt: off or fmt: skip comment kept a JavaScript or CSS region unformatted, as requested.
diagnostics.when: A fmt: off or fmt: skip directive covers an embedded JavaScript or CSS region.
diagnostics.fix: Nothing to fix. Remove the directive if you want the region formatted.

diagnostics.title: Embedded language unsupported
diagnostics.summary: A <script> or <style> region declares a language Citry has no formatter for, so it was left unchanged.
diagnostics.when: An embedded script or style region declares a language that no Citry formatter handles.
diagnostics.fix: Nothing to fix. Format that region with its own tools.

diagnostics.title: Embedded interpolation unsupported
diagnostics.summary: A JavaScript or CSS region contains Citry interpolation, such as {{ title }}, so it was left unchanged.
diagnostics.when: An embedded JavaScript or CSS region contains Citry interpolation, which an external formatter cannot handle safely.
diagnostics.fix: Pass the value through js_data() or css_data() instead of interpolating it, or leave the region unformatted.

diagnostics.title: Embedded formatter unavailable
diagnostics.summary: No JavaScript or CSS formatter answered, so that region was left unchanged.
diagnostics.when: Citry asks the editor to format embedded JavaScript or CSS, and no installed formatter returns an edit.
diagnostics.fix: In VS Code, check that Prettier for VS Code is installed and enabled for the language, or disable it so Citry uses its own copy of Prettier.

diagnostics.title: Invalid Python host syntax
diagnostics.summary: The Python file has a syntax error, so Citry could not find the component strings to format.
diagnostics.when: A format command targets a Python file that is not valid Python.
diagnostics.fix: Fix the Python syntax error, then format again.

diagnostics.title: Document is not eligible for formatting
diagnostics.summary: The file or cursor position is not inside a Citry template, script, or style, so there is nothing to format.
diagnostics.when: Citry cannot tell that the document or cursor position belongs to a template, js, or css string, or a standalone Citry template.
diagnostics.fix: Place the cursor inside a template, js, or css string, or open the template file itself.

diagnostics.title: Document changed during formatting
diagnostics.summary: The document changed while Citry was formatting it, so the result was discarded.
diagnostics.when: The document changes after Citry prepares the edit and before the editor applies it.
diagnostics.fix: Run the format command again.

diagnostics.title: Formatting cancelled
diagnostics.summary: Formatting was cancelled before Citry applied it.
diagnostics.when: The editor or you cancel a format request before Citry applies its edits.
diagnostics.fix: Nothing to fix. Run the format command again if needed.
